next.t: Martin County, Florida, holds its final vote on a one-year moratorium, and Pulaski County, Arkansas, may vote to override its judge's veto of data center rules.
Lexington's data center pause expires unless the council extends it.
Election Day: 36 governor races, the Ohio Senate race, Public Service Commission seats in Georgia and Louisiana, and 35+ local data center measures from Ohio to Maine.
Charlotte's 150-day moratorium expires unless extended; city staff recommended extending it.
Virginia work group reports on data center taxation ahead of the 2027 session.
PJM targets its FERC filing for a flexible large-load service model.
Loudoun County's final vote on a 12-month pause in the world's densest data center market.
Meriwether County, Georgia's extended moratorium ends.
Nashville's data center permit pause ends.
Air permit hearing for New Mexico's Project Jupiter in Sunland Park.
ERCOT's target for finishing the Texas audit, and Louisiana regulators' expected vote on gas plants for Meta's Hyperion expansion.
Coweta County, Georgia, and Snohomish County, Washington, pauses expire unless renewed.
Hochul's deadline to sign or veto the Responsible Data Center Development Act; inaction is a pocket veto. Massachusetts must also set its clean-energy payment for data centers.
Most of California's seven data center laws take effect, and 2027 sessions open with moratorium bills in Virginia and Georgia and incentive fights in Texas.
Maine's state recommendations on large data centers are due.
PJM's first capacity auction without the price cap.
Oregon's permit and state land pauses end. Ohio ban amendment organizers need 413,488 signatures by about this time for the Nov 2027 ballot.
Virginia's consumption tax sunsets unless extended.

gaps.p: Local moratorium tallies range from 313 (Urban Institute) to 632 jurisdictions taking action (GatherGov) to 933 local actions (Gizmo Warehouse map). The gap is mostly definitions: adopted pauses vs. proposals vs. denials vs. zoning conditions.
Trackers log the vote but rarely follow up. Of 28 well-documented blocked fights since 2023, one map found 13 still pending or in court and four delayed then built anyway.
On-site gas turbines dodge grid queues and, under EPA proposals, some public comment. Texas only closed the gap with a second order. Few trackers follow air permits.
The White House pledge covers companies delivering most U.S. power, but enforcement sits with state utility commissions. No one is systematically checking signers' tariffs against their promises.
Texas found as few as 28% of data centers answered its water survey. California's new reporting starts in 2027. Consumption, not discharge, is what states are now trying to measure.
Tribal nations in Oklahoma are acting on their own lands, while Texas lawmakers and courts in California and Mississippi are testing how far local bans can go. Both fronts are thinly covered.
